approval_status_current: Approved and marketed: US NDA 203284 (2016), EU authorised, Japan (2025-12-22); pediatric labeling (see Drug_Evidence_and_Regulatory_Status.md)
direction_of_action: Stabilize destabilized missense BUBR1 (the proband's missense allele) to raise steady-state abundance; active moiety phenylacetate (prodrug triglyceride)
pharmacological_evidence: Chemical-chaperone stabilization of misfolded client proteins (CFTR F508del models); BUBR1-specific stabilization UNTESTED
alignment_with_modeled_intervention: Direct: raises the exact pool the atlas identifies as the dominant lever (abundance, not specific activity)
off_target_and_mitotic_concerns: Hepatotoxicity signal (label); QTc <10 ms at submaximal exposure; systemic exposure at labeled UCD doses is high (PAA Cmax ~48.5 ug/mL for sodium PBA)
evidence_in_bubr1_deficiency_or_mva: Suijkerbuijk 2010: abundance rescue of OTHER MVA1 variants restored checkpoint function; no BUBR1-specific stabilization data
verdict: CONDITIONAL, quantitatively plausible (Table 6): model requires pool x1.8 for partial rescue (S>=0.75) and x3.5 for near-WT (S>=0.90) in D1; protein-stabilization analogy bounds for phenylbutyrates (other client proteins) are 1.5-4.8x, i.e., the required multiplier sits inside the analogy range; the BUB1B-specific stabilization magnitude is unmeasured, so the verdict is conditional on that assay (three-outcome framework, outcome 3)

model_mechanism: Restore functional BUBR1:Bub3 pool via nonsense-allele readthrough
model_target_and_direction: Increase full-length BUBR1 from the the proband's nonsense allele allele (NMD block + readthrough)
evidence_from_atlas: as above (pool restoration is the dominant lever regardless of allele of origin)
approval_status_current: NOT marketed anywhere checked (US discontinued; Japan Solfa discontinued 2017; Ireland withdrawn 2019); historical US/Japan approvals only
direction_of_action: Block NMD and read through the TGA stop to make full-length BUBR1 from the nonsense allele
pharmacological_evidence: NMD block + readthrough demonstrated in other genes (Gonzalez-Hilarion 2012; Atanasova 2017); BUB1B readthrough UNTESTED; class-level negative: ataluren EMA authorisation not renewed 2025-03-28 after failed confirmatory trials; quantitative readthrough bound: best-supported human readthrough drug produces ~10% of WT full-length protein per allele (ataluren CFTR R1014X: 10.3%; amlexanox FANCA: ~9%)
alignment_with_modeled_intervention: Direct: the model does not distinguish allele of origin for the pool lever; readthrough is the only route that can rescue the null allele
off_target_and_mitotic_concerns: NMD modulation is transcription-circuit-wide (global off-target potential); mitotic toxicity not characterized in patient cells; readthrough efficiency stop/context dependent
verdict: QUANTITATIVELY INSUFFICIENT as monotherapy (Table 6, outcome 2): best-supported readthrough ~10% WT full-length adds <=1.2x-1.6x to the 0.055 uM trans pool vs >=1.8x required for partial rescue; retained only as a combinatorial contributor; BUB1B-specific readthrough measurement required (outcome 3)

alignment_with_modeled_intervention: Partial; the model EXCLUDES Cdc20-elevation strategies as disease-adjacent
verdict: NEGATIVE/EXCLUDED - model-driven negative result: Cdc20-based strategies are not defensible for this disease model

model_target_and_direction: All panel checkpoint proteins: BUB1B, BUB3, MAD2L1, TRIP13, CUL1 (SCF scaffold), ANAPC1/2, APC11/ANAPC11, PTTG1 (securin), CDC20, CDC25C, UBE2C, PDS5A/B (cohesin regulators), CDK1, BUB1, AURKA/B, PLK1, KIF11, CEP57, CDCA7
evidence_from_atlas: 22-target screen of DGIdb, Open Targets, ChEMBL (via DGIdb), FDA Drugs@FDA/DailyMed/EMA labels (accessed 2026-10-23; annotation-corrected: PTTG1 added as the true securin and APC11/ANAPC11 as the APC/C Cul1-family scaffold, PDS5A/B correctly annotated as cohesin regulators not securin, CUL1 annotated as SCF scaffold not APC/C): 17 approved entities (16 molecules) with direct molecular activity on the mitotic apparatus, ALL on TUBB (taxanes, epothilone, eribulin, vinca alkaloids, colchicine, maytansinoid/auristatin ADC payloads); ZERO approved drugs with a checkpoint-signaling protein as approved target; gap list per-target with sources
approval_status_current: Approved (indicated for oncology, and colchicine for gout/FMF)
pharmacological_evidence: Direct TUBB binding with primary-structure evidence (Schiff 1979; Himes 1976; Okouneva 2008, PMID 18645010; MMAE PMID 33852878)
alignment_with_modeled_intervention: NOT aligned with the modeled intervention direction: the model's beneficial lever is RESTORING BUBR1-dependent checkpoint signaling, while microtubule poisons cause mitotic arrest/CIN - the direction the addendum warns against treating as therapeutic in a disease whose problem is checkpoint insufficiency plus aneuploidy
off_target_and_mitotic_concerns: Profound mitotic toxicity (myelosuppression, neuropathy); would aggravate, not relieve, the aneuploidy burden; systemic exposure in a child is the defining safety concern
verdict: EXCLUDED - the only approved drugs acting on the mitotic apparatus are microtubule poisons; none reproduces a modeled beneficial perturbation, and their pharmacology is the opposite direction of the required intervention
